#TIP_TAB_CONNECTION: Connect to the RM10 and watch its viewer state.
#TIP_TAB_DISPLAYS: View displays and set the slot lock.
#TIP_TAB_SETTINGS: Language, theme, tray and data locations.
#NOTE_IP: The app connects to the IP you enter; no discovery. The certificate dates are invalid, so only the SHA-256 fingerprint is checked.
#NOTE_DETECTION: Reads /api/streamer and the session log. When the screen is off, a new session in the log is the wake-up. Missing data is treated as unknown, never guessed.
#REASON_LOG_ONLY: no signal; no new session in the log
#LABEL_HDR: Turn system HDR on after restore
#NOTE_LOCK: Two binding modes: Screen N follows the connector slot (DP=1, HDMI/DVI=2) and survives EDID/name/target-id changes; Follow display binds the current target id, so the KVM follows that display. On this machine the physical display is 1 and the KVM is 2. "Not locked" means detection only.
#ERR_AUTH_EMPTY: Enter the username and password first.
#ERR_PIN_MISSING: Test the connection and trust the certificate first.
#ERR_AUTOSTART: Could not write the startup entry.
#TRAY_MINIMIZED: Minimized to tray; detection continues in the background.
#TIP_IP: LAN IP of the RM10; no auto-discovery.
#TIP_PASSWORD: KVM web login password; stored with DPAPI.
#TIP_TEST: Test TLS, certificate fingerprint and login.
#TIP_POLL: How often to read the viewer state.
#TIP_AUTO: Start detection automatically when the app launches.
#TIP_MINIMIZE: Hide to the system tray when closing.
#TIP_AUTOSTART: Write the current user's logon startup entry.
#TIP_APPLY: Capture the current desktop as the recorded display snapshot (used when applying it).
#TIP_LOCK: Two bindings: Screen N follows the connector slot and survives EDID/name/target-id changes; Follow display binds the current target id. "Not locked" means detection only.
#TIP_ON_CONNECT_KVM_ONLY: Keep the KVM screen only; the physical screen goes dark.
#TIP_ON_CONNECT_CLONE: Same image on both screens; HDR is turned off.
#TIP_ON_CONNECT_EXTEND: Use the KVM screen as a secondary display.
#TIP_ON_DISCONNECT_RESTORE: Restore the most recently captured local snapshot.
#TIP_ON_DISCONNECT_SCREEN: Switch to a fixed Windows display number.
#TIP_ON_DISCONNECT_CLONE: Same image on both screens; HDR off.
#TIP_ON_DISCONNECT_HOLD: Stay in the remote layout until you switch manually.
#TIP_SCREEN: Display number to keep after disconnect.
#TIP_HDR: Affects only the restore action; it does not change the HDR state recorded in the captured snapshot.
#TIP_SNAPSHOT: The actual captured display state; the HDR option only controls the restore action.
#TIP_CLEAR_LOG: Clear the in-window log; the files on disk are kept.
#DISP_ERR_NO_KVM: Lock the KVM display on the Displays page first.
#DISP_ERR_NO_SNAPSHOT: No valid recorded display snapshot; refusing to switch. Capture one on the Actions page first.
#DISP_ERR_INVALID_SNAPSHOT: The recorded display snapshot is invalid; refusing to switch.
#DISP_ERR_REMOTE_LAYOUT: The current layout is remote; cannot capture it as local.
#DISP_ERR_CAPTURE: Could not capture the display configuration.
#TIP_RESTORE: Apply the recorded display snapshot exactly. If it was single/duplicate/extend, that layout is applied; it is not always just screen 1.
#TIP_AUTO_APPLY: Master switch: when on, the connect/disconnect actions run automatically; when off, only detection runs.
#TIP_DISPLAY_TABLE: Connected displays; roles follow the slot lock.
#TIP_DISPLAY_STATUS: Current topology and KVM lock state.
#NOTE_GUARD_MASTER: When on, the connect/disconnect actions below run automatically. When off, the app only detects viewers and never switches displays.
#ABOUT: Windows service + session-1 display agent + named pipe; the GUI is config/status only. Logon/lock/sleep/shutdown paths are wired; a final logon-screen check is recommended.
#NOTE_ACTIONS: When the master switch is off, only detection runs. When on, connect/disconnect actions execute automatically and roll back on failure.
#NOTE_DISPLAYS: Display reading and switching are enabled; the slot lock follows the connector, not the EDID name.
#TIP_SERVICE_START: Start the GLKVMGuard service. Windows will request Administrator approval (UAC).
#TIP_SERVICE_STOP: Stop the GLKVMGuard service. Detection stops and the service makes a best-effort local restore; requires Administrator approval.
#TIP_SERVICE_UNINSTALL: Uninstall the GLKVMGuard service. User config/logs/snapshots are preserved; requires Administrator approval.
#NOTE_SERVICE_CONTROL: Start, stop, and uninstall require Administrator approval. Uninstall removes the service config and machine-scope password but preserves user data; run install_service.ps1 to reinstall.
#CONFIRM_STOP_SERVICE_TEXT: Stopping GLKVMGuard stops background detection and automatic switching. The service will make a best-effort local restore. Continue?
#CONFIRM_UNINSTALL_SERVICE_TEXT: This stops and removes the GLKVMGuard service, service.json, and the machine-scope password. User config, logs, and snapshots are preserved. You will need install_service.ps1 to reinstall. Continue?
#ERR_SERVICE_NOT_INSTALLED: The Windows service is not installed. Run install_service.ps1 first.
#STATUS_SERVICE_ACTION_RUNNING: Waiting for Administrator approval and running the service action…
#SERVICE_UNINSTALLED_TEXT: The GLKVMGuard service was removed. User config, logs, and snapshots are preserved. Run install_service.ps1 to reinstall. The GUI can now run standalone.
